intro: Readers judge a book by its cover in the half-second it shows up in search results. PiCraft designs genre-appropriate covers with your title and author name set in type that reads at thumbnail size.
Download a 1600×2560 px eBook cover for Kindle and other stores, and a 6×9 inch front cover with bleed for your paperback designer.

faq.q: Can I use these covers on Amazon KDP?
faq.a: Yes. The eBook file matches KDP's ideal 1600×2560 px, as a JPG in RGB. KDP also asks you to tell it when content is AI-generated, so check its current content guidelines when you publish.

faq.q: Does it make the spine and back cover?
faq.a: No. You get a front cover; paperback wraps depend on page count and are best assembled in your printer's template.
Genres have strong visual conventions. A thriller that looks like a romance confuses readers and hurts sales.
The text is part of the image. To change it, generate again with the new wording.

faq.q: Is the cover big enough for print?
faq.a: The paperback front is 6.125×9.25 inches at 300 DPI, which includes bleed for a 6×9 inch book. For other trim sizes, ask your printer for a template and scale the front accordingly.

faq.q: Can I use it for stores other than Amazon?
faq.a: The 1600×2560 px eBook cover is a common size for eBook stores, but each store has its own rules, so check the current requirements before you upload.

faq.q: How do I make the title readable as a thumbnail?
faq.a: Use a short title and check the image at about 160 px tall. If you can't read the title, shorten it or generate again.

faq.q: Can I describe the cover image?
faq.a: Yes. The cover idea field takes a scene or a symbol of up to 300 characters. Leave it empty and PiCraft chooses an image that fits the genre.

faq.q: Can I keep one look across a series?
faq.a: Choose the same genre and describe a similar kind of image for each book. Results are consistent but not identical, so review each cover.

We don't claim ownership of the files you generate, and you may use them commercially under our terms. AI-generated images may not qualify for copyright protection in some countries, so consider a designer if you need a cover that is legally unique.
